before: Result carries either a success value or a typed failure value. Creating it does not start a task, throw immediately or make an operation asynchronous.

EntryProblem conforms to Error and has two named cases. checkedName validates a String: isEmpty identifies no characters; count is the Character count, not UTF-8 bytes. Result<String, EntryProblem> fixes its two payload types. .success(text) wraps accepted text, while .failure(.missing) stores the failure. describe consumes that value using an exhaustive switch; let name binds the success payload. Here no try is needed because neither function throws.
Optional practice: Return the correct stored success or failure and describe all three paths. Predict a different input before running.
after: Result is a value that holds either success or failure. It lets you keep an outcome and inspect it later. Storing a failure does not throw an error by itself.
Result<String, EntryProblem> holds a String for success or an EntryProblem for failure. .success(text) keeps accepted text. .failure(...) keeps the reason the text was rejected.

switch reads which outcome is stored. let name gives a name to the successful text. The two failure cases each get a message. These functions return values without throwing, so their calls do not need try.
